cases.sentence: После ___ и большого количества коньяку, выпитого у Бартнянского, Степан Аркадьич, только немного опоздав против назначенного времени, входил к графине Лидии Ивановне.
cases.explain: «прекрасного обеда» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: After a capital dinner and a great deal of cognac drunk at Bartnyansky’s, Stepan Arkadyevitch, only a little later than the appointed time, went in to Countess Lidia Ivanovna’s.

cases.sentence: После прекрасного обеда и ___ коньяку, выпитого у Бартнянского, Степан Аркадьич, только немного опоздав против назначенного времени, входил к графине Лидии Ивановне.
cases.explain: «большого количества» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: After a capital dinner and a great deal of cognac drunk at Bartnyansky’s, Stepan Arkadyevitch, only a little later than the appointed time, went in to Countess Lidia Ivanovna’s.

cases.sentence: – Я вас познакомила с ним как с Landau, – сказала она ___, взглянув на француза и потом тотчас на Алексея Александровича, – но он, собственно, граф Беззубов, как вы, вероятно, знаете.
cases.explain: «тихим голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I introduced you to him as Landau,” she said in a soft voice, glancing at the Frenchman and again immediately after at Alexey Alexandrovitch, “but he is really Count Bezzubov, as you’re probably aware. Only he does not like the title.”

cases.sentence: Наступило ___, после которого графиня Лидия Ивановна, как бы приступая к главному предмету разговора, с тонкой улыбкой сказала Облонскому:
cases.explain: «минутное молчание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A moment’s silence followed, after which Countess Lidia Ivanovna, as though approaching the main topic of conversation, said with a fine smile to Oblonsky:

cases.sentence: Наступило минутное молчание, после которого графиня Лидия Ивановна, как бы приступая к ___ разговора, с тонкой улыбкой сказала Облонскому:
cases.explain: «главному предмету» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: A moment’s silence followed, after which Countess Lidia Ivanovna, as though approaching the main topic of conversation, said with a fine smile to Oblonsky:

cases.sentence: Наступило минутное молчание, после которого графиня Лидия Ивановна, как бы приступая к главному предмету разговора, с ___ сказала Облонскому:
cases.explain: «тонкой улыбкой» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: A moment’s silence followed, after which Countess Lidia Ivanovna, as though approaching the main topic of conversation, said with a fine smile to Oblonsky:

cases.sentence: Вы понимаете, о чем я говорю, – сказала она, поднимая свои прекрасные ___.
cases.explain: «задумчивые глаза» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I’ve known you for a long while, and am very glad to make a closer acquaintance with you. Les amis de nos amis sont nos amis. But to be a true friend, one must enter into the spiritual state of one’s friend, and I fear that you are not doing so in the case of Alexey Alexandrovitch. You understand what I mean?” she said, lifting her fine pensive eyes.

cases.sentence: – То есть я в ___ могу представить себе эту перемену.
cases.explain: «общих чертах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Oh, well, in general outlines I can conceive the change. We have always been friendly, and now. …” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, responding with a sympathetic glance to the expression of the countess, and mentally balancing the question with which of the two ministers she was most intimate, so as to know about which to ask her to speak for him.

cases.sentence: Мы всегда были дружны, и теперь… – отвечая ___ на взгляд графини, сказал Степан Аркадьич, соображая, с которым из двух министров она ближе, чтобы знать, о ком из двух придется просить ее.
cases.explain: «нежным взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Oh, well, in general outlines I can conceive the change. We have always been friendly, and now. …” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, responding with a sympathetic glance to the expression of the countess, and mentally balancing the question with which of the two ministers she was most intimate, so as to know about which to ask her to speak for him.

cases.sentence: – О, конечно, графиня, – сказал он, – но я думаю, что эти перемены так интимны, что никто, даже самый 6___, не любит говорить.
cases.explain: «лизкий человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, of course, countess,” he said; “but I imagine such changes are a matter so private that no one, even the most intimate friend, would care to speak of them.”

cases.sentence: – Не может быть разницы в деле ___.
cases.explain: «святой истины» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “There can be no difference where it is a question of holy truth.”

cases.sentence: – То есть вы хотите сказать, что грех мешает ему? – сказала Лидия Ивановна. – Но это ___.
cases.explain: «ложное мнение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That is, you mean that sin keeps him back?” said Lidia Ivanovna. “But that is a false idea. There is no sin for believers, their sin has been atoned for. Pardon,” she added, looking at the footman, who came in again with another letter. She read it and gave a verbal answer: “Tomorrow at the Grand Duchess’s, say.” “For the believer sin is not,” she went on.

cases.sentence: Греха нет для верующих, грех уже искуплен. Pardon, – прибавила она, глядя на опять вошедшего с ___ лакея.
cases.explain: «другой запиской» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “That is, you mean that sin keeps him back?” said Lidia Ivanovna. “But that is a false idea. There is no sin for believers, their sin has been atoned for. Pardon,” she added, looking at the footman, who came in again with another letter. She read it and gave a verbal answer: “Tomorrow at the Grand Duchess’s, say.” “For the believer sin is not,” she went on.

cases.sentence: Она прочла и на словах ответила: – Завтра у ___, скажите. – Для верующего нет греха, – продолжала она разговор.
cases.explain: «великой княгини» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “That is, you mean that sin keeps him back?” said Lidia Ivanovna. “But that is a false idea. There is no sin for believers, their sin has been atoned for. Pardon,” she added, looking at the footman, who came in again with another letter. She read it and gave a verbal answer: “Tomorrow at the Grand Duchess’s, say.” “For the believer sin is not,” she went on.

cases.sentence: – Трудиться для бога, трудами, постом спасать душу, – с ___ сказала графиня Лидия Ивановна, – это дикие понятия наших монахов…
cases.explain: «гадливым презрением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Striving for God, saving the soul by fasting,” said Countess Lidia Ivanovna, with disgusted contempt, “those are the crude ideas of our monks. … Yet that is nowhere said. It is far simpler and easier,” she added, looking at Oblonsky with the same encouraging smile with which at court she encouraged youthful maids of honor, disconcerted by the new surroundings of the court.

cases.sentence: – Трудиться для бога, трудами, постом спасать душу, – с гадливым презрением сказала графиня Лидия Ивановна, – это ___ наших монахов…
cases.explain: «дикие понятия» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Striving for God, saving the soul by fasting,” said Countess Lidia Ivanovna, with disgusted contempt, “those are the crude ideas of our monks. … Yet that is nowhere said. It is far simpler and easier,” she added, looking at Oblonsky with the same encouraging smile with which at court she encouraged youthful maids of honor, disconcerted by the new surroundings of the court.

cases.sentence: – Vous comprenez l'anglais? – спросила Лидия Ивановна и, получив ___, встала и начала перебирать на полочке книги.
cases.explain: «утвердительный ответ» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Vous comprenez l’anglais?” asked Lidia Ivanovna, and receiving a reply in the affirmative, she got up and began looking through a shelf of books.

cases.sentence: Скажите, завтра в два часа. – Да, – сказала она, заложив пальцем место в книге и со вздохом взглянув пред собой задумчивыми ___. – Вот как действует вера настоящая.
cases.explain: «прекрасными глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I want to read him Safe and Happy, or Under the Wing,” she said, looking inquiringly at Karenin. And finding the book, and sitting down again in her place, she opened it. “It’s very short. In it is described the way by which faith can be reached, and the happiness, above all earthly bliss, with which it fills the soul. The believer cannot be unhappy because he is not alone. But you will see.” She was just settling herself to read when the footman came in again. “Madame Borozdina? Tell her, tomorrow at two o’clock. Yes,” she said, putting her finger in the place in the book, and gazing before her with her fine pensive eyes, “that is how true faith acts. You know Marie Sanina? You know about her trouble? She lost her only child. She was in despair. And what happened? She found this comforter, and she thanks God now for the death of her child. Such is the happiness faith brings!”
